verified_technical_facts: The user runs DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3 (bundled runtime) with provider commandcode (@mars-sea/dsh-commandcode-provider@0.15.4) and model deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash. The dsh CLI on PATH is 0.1.5-rc.1 and is NOT what the user actually runs.

The commandcode plugin declares dsh compatibility >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.2.2-0, so it cannot be used on 0.1.5; an incompatible plugin is skipped silently and the runtime falls back to another provider (observed: deepseek-official -> HTTP 402).
Every probe must assert request/header.config.provider and .model, otherwise a provider fallback is mistaken for a model failure.
DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 SDK protocol methods: initialize, session/prompt, session/resume, session/wait, session/working-directory/get|set, shutdown. No cancel, no approve, no session/close.
session/resume on 0.2.1 restores conversation history across a full process restart (verified by token recall); 0.1.5 has no resume and rejects sessionId reuse with already exists.
MCP is the only tool-registration path; on 0.2.1 the model really invoked mcp__studio__get_studio_health and the Studio server recorded tools/call + tools/call.served.
Process reclamation must be three-state (PRESENT/ABSENT/CHECK_FAILED); a failed query is never evidence of absence. Orphan matching needs command-line markers, not just the parent-child chain.
A process check must exclude its own enumeration process (unique sentinel) and conhost.exe, or it observes itself and reports a phantom leftover.
dsh-atomic-write never checks whether the lock-holder pid is alive; a dead-pid profiles/node_modules.lock makes the next boot fail after a 2000 ms deadline, surfaced only as JSON-RPC input closed.
Startup time is bimodal: 2-3 s warm vs 73-128 s when profiles/node_modules must be rebuilt (187 entries, 164 symlinks); the SDK default initializeTimeoutMs of 10 s is unusable.
This host injects a safe-delete shim via NODE_OPTIONS that can abort DSH profile maintenance with SAFE_DELETE_BULK_CONFIRM_REQUIRED; that is environment interference, not a runtime defect.

Patch files use two shapes: insert: for new rows, a bare id: row to override an existing row. Inserting llm-commandcode alone does not change the default model; agent-default-model must be overridden too.

A redaction gate must be falsifiable: the first two versions of scrub-evidence.mjs reported "0 residual" because the Windows pattern required two backslashes while decoded paths have one, and because only four directories were scanned. It now scans git-tracked files (152), parses JSON first, and is validated by planting a leak and confirming exit 1.

Scripted string replacement can silently comment out code: a literal //n (an un-escaped newline) made // swallow the first route assertion in CC-3 and CC-4, so only the second run/turn was checked while the report claimed both were. Read back and assert on actual values after any scripted edit.

fs.cpSync and bulk fs.rmSync terminate this node process with exit 127 and no message under the host safe-delete shim; manual recursive copy works and npm ci is unaffected. Setup therefore never deletes a tree.

A dependency fingerprint is not a lockfile. profile-locks/<profile>/package-lock.json is a real npm lockfile used by npm ci; a version that disagrees with it raises DependencyDriftError and aborts the run.
CC-0 is a CLI probe and emits no request/header event, so it cannot prove which provider served the request. Only CC-1..CC-4 carry route assertions.
Each probe run so far observed exactly one request/header per turn, including the tool-using CC-2, so multi-hop (tool call then second request) route coverage is still unobserved.
